one_month_reasoning: Reddit has NOT announced its Q3 2026 date: EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-08-12, and only TipRanks calls Nov 4 (after close, outside the window) 'confirmed'. Reddit's own pattern is Thursday at month end (8-Ks 2025-10-30, 2026-04-30, 2026-07-30), which points to Thu Oct 29, inside the window. I put ~57% on the earnings reaction landing inside the window (round 1: 0%). Inside the window as well: Alphabet and Meta Q3 prints (late Oct) for ad-demand and AI-search/referral read-through, and any Google/OpenAI licensing-renewal headline (only $62.0M of licensing RPO falls in rest-of-2026 per the 10-Q, so the renewal is due). Earnings direction is not predictable: Q1/Q2 beat the top of guidance by ~10-11% yet the stock fell 12-21% on the Q2 print over flat US DAUq, and the logged-in split is dropped from Q3, which may unsettle. So I keep the center at spot (tiny +0.3% drift) and widen the spread: mixture of a 57% earnings-in-window component (sigma ~22% = sqrt(14% base^2 + 17% earnings gap^2)) and a 43% no-event component (sigma 14%). Net it is near-symmetric but with fatter tails than round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend 60% P/E (horizon NTM taxed adjusted EPS $9.03 x 17.5x = $158) and 40% SBC-adjusted FCF yield (NTM owner FCF $1.47B at 5.0% + $3.5B net cash over 207M diluted shares = $159). Round 1 was $169; the cut comes from taxing the EPS, 207M shares and the 5.0% yield, partly offset by dropping the separate 10% risk haircut.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: CY27 non-GAAP EPS $9.69 grossed to pretax $9.81, taxed at 20% = $7.85; CY28 +20% = $9.42; NTM at Oct-2027 = 0.25x7.85 + 0.75x9.42 = $9.03; x 17.5x = $158. No extra cash add-on (peer P/Es also embed their cash; RDDT EPS includes ~$0.5/share interest income).

inputs_detail.input: CY2027 street EPS (non-GAAP, SBC excluded, nearly untaxed)
inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis states 'EPS and Forward PE are based on non-GAAP adjusted numbers'; same basis as all 11 peers.

H1'26 tax was $5.7M on $462.6M pretax (1.2%) because of a full US valuation allowance whose release the 10-Q discusses. Peers' EPS is taxed, so RDDT must be too. 21% federal statutory plus state, less deductions for SBC, gives ~20%. NOLs keep cash tax lower, which is handled in the FCF method.
Street EPS growth falls from 69% (2026) to 26% (2027). MAGNA sees social ad growth slowing to single digits from 2027, so I assume a further step down to ~20%.

11-peer CY2027 non-GAAP median 17.6x (range 7.3-38.6x). I use the median, with no premium or discount. A premium for 32% revenue growth is not shown to persist, given search-referral dependence (10-Q), flat US DAUq and the licensing renewal. A discount is not warranted either: the balance sheet is net cash and margins are top quartile. I dropped round 1's separate 10% EPS haircut so the same risk is not counted twice; the traffic risk sits in the bear scenario.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: CY27 rev $4.46B x 46% adj EBITDA = $2.05B, less ~10% cash tax and ~$5M capex, less SBC 13% of revenue ($0.58B) = $1.26B owner FCF; CY28 +22% = $1.54B; NTM at horizon ~$1.47B / 5.0% = $29.4B + $3.5B net cash = $32.9B / 207M = $159

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2'26 42.6%, Q3 guide ~45%, long-term target 50%; take 46%.
Q2'26 SBC $101M on $805M revenue (12.5%); CFO guides low-to-mid teens. Treated as a real cost.
NOLs and SBC deductions keep cash tax well below the 20% book rate through 2028.
In line with the ~20% EPS step-down plus modest margin leverage.
20x owner FCF, inside the peer P/E range: between the 17.6x peer median (5.7%) and META/GOOGL at 21-23x (4.3-4.7%). Round 1 used 4.5%, which implied a premium I cannot show persists.
$2,786M today, no debt, plus ~5 quarters of FCF ($261M in Q2 alone) less ~$235M a quarter of buybacks.
Fully diluted 207.0M at 2026-06-30, +0.2% YoY; buybacks offset SBC. Round 1 wrongly used 195M.

bear.story: AI Mode and search-algorithm changes keep cutting logged-out traffic, US DAUq declines, and the Google licensing deal lapses (licensing RPO is small, but losing it signals a worse traffic relationship). 2027 growth fades toward ~15-20%, NTM taxed EPS is ~$7.0, and the market pays ~12x plus ~$17/share net cash.

base.story: Ad pricing and advertiser growth carry 2027 revenue ~+30% to consensus $4.46B despite flat US users. Margins reach 46-47%. The stock trades at the 17.5x peer median on ~$9.0-9.2 NTM taxed EPS.

bull.story: Beats over the top of guidance continue (~10% in Q1/Q2), the licensing deal renews on usage-based terms and US logged-in users re-accelerate. NTM taxed EPS is ~$10.3 and the multiple moves to ~22x, the GOOGL/META level and the upper middle of the peer range.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 P/E 7.3x (SNAP) to 38.6x (ROKU); interquartile ~8.9x-23.0x. 11 peers on one basis: StockAnalysis CY2027 non-GAAP consensus EPS, all December fiscal years, so calendar-aligned; prices 2026-10-05; SPOT EPS converted from EUR at ~1.17. Ex-ROKU (EPS still inflecting) the 10-peer median is 15.6x. META/GOOGL consensus is effectively GAAP (SBC expensed), the others are SBC-excluded. Forward EV/EBITDA was not collected on a consistent basis, so it is left null, and no method relies on it.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: On the same basis RDDT trades at 15.7x untaxed CY27 non-GAAP EPS, or about 19.3x once that EPS is taxed at 20% ($151.69/$7.85): roughly 10% above the median. I apply 17.5x, at the median, to taxed horizon NTM EPS.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: None applied. RDDT's revenue growth (+32% CY27) and margins (~46% adj EBITDA) are above the peer median, and it has net cash, which argues for a premium. But the persistence of that growth through Oct 2027 is not established: the 10-Q ties DAUq to third-party search-algorithm changes, US DAUq was flat QoQ, logged-in/out disclosure ends in Q3, and licensing RPO falls from $62.0M (rest of 2026) to $30.1M (2027). Heavy SBC (~13% of revenue) is also excluded from RDDT's adjusted EPS but not from META's or GOOGL's. Sell-side outperformance calls are not used. So the median is the multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $100 is ~16% below the 52-week low. It equals ~10.6x taxed CY27 adjusted EPS ex ~$17/share net cash, the bottom quartile of the peer range alongside SNAP/PINS/MTCH, which grow at a third of Reddit's rate. A price that low would most likely mean user/traffic loss had become visible in revenue (growth toward 15% or less, US DAUq falling for several quarters, Google cutting both referrals and licensing), not ordinary 70%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 2 corrections from the supervisor, which I verified in the Q2 press release and 10-Q: 207.0M diluted shares (not 195M); consensus EPS is nearly untaxed (H1 tax $5.7M on $462.6M pretax); the $43M is total Other revenue, not licensing (licensing RPO $92.1M, of which $62.0M is in rest-of-2026); and the Q3 date is unconfirmed (no 8-K, Thursday month-end pattern). I tax CY27 non-GAAP EPS at 20% ($7.85), roll to NTM at the horizon ($9.03) and apply the 11-peer median 17.5x, with no premium (growth persistence unproven, given search dependence) and no discount (net cash, top margins). The P/E gives $158, SBC-adjusted FCF at a 5.0% yield gives $159, and the blend is $158, about 4% above spot. My figure is below the supervisor's $168 because I use a 20% tax rate and CY28 growth of +20% (their $9.65 NTM implies a lower tax rate or faster growth); I checked their inputs rather than adopting them. Industry read-through is unchanged: ad demand is healthy (Meta price/ad +12%, Snap pricing +10%), MAGNA expects social ad growth to slow from 2027, and the traffic chain (Similarweb, a single-panel estimate of ~57% organic search; AI Mode referral rates) is the main risk. Scenarios are 100/160/230 at 27/50/23, giving a mean of $159.9, which reconciles with the $158 fair value (the $2 gap is bull-side skew from the beat history). The ladder is a mixture of lognormals around those scenarios with an effective log-vol of ~47%, below the 70% realized (inflated by the July -21% and August S&P-inclusion jumps) but well above a typical large cap. The median is ~$147, below spot, because of that right-skewed spread, and P(>=152) is 0.47. One month: ~57% that earnings land in the window, so the spread is wider but centered at spot.
